title: Income/balance/cashflow statements for BSE SME CHTR (Chatterbox Technologies) silently serve Charter Communications Inc. (US, NASDAQ:CHTR) data instead
repro: curl 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/CHTR/income' (or /balance, /cashflow) while region=IN / for a BSE-SME-registered symbol 'CHTR' -> returns a statement with periods 2021-12-31..2025-12-31, symbol echoed as bare 'CHTR' (no exchange suffix), total_revenue ~51-55 BILLION, basic_earnings_per_share ~36-37, weighted_average_basic_shares_outstanding ~126-165 million, provider='openbb-mcp'. These are Charter Communications, Inc.'s (US cable co, ~$70B market cap) actual reported financials, not Chatterbox Technologies Ltd's (Indian BSE-SME influencer-marketing agency, market cap ~Rs 54 crore, Rs 84.22 crore revenue, ~1.41 crore shares). Reproduced from the 2026-09-19 collected snapshot: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P3_CHTR.json calls 'income'/'balance'/'cashflow'.
evidence: sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:495-498 (get_income_statement passes validate=None, no correctness/region gate, unlike get_fundamentals at 473-491 which is given _fundamentals_validator + accept=_fundamentals_screener_complete + fallback_ok=_fundamentals_has_data), sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:502-505 (get_balance_sheet, same validate=None), sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:509-512 (get_cash_flow, same); sidecar/services/openbb_mcp_provider.py:260-262 (_normalize_symbol only does '.'->'-' + uppercase — no exchange-suffix/region resolution, unlike yfinance_provider._yahoo_symbol used by get_fundamentals), sidecar/services/openbb_mcp_provider.py:448-483 (_financial_statement/get_income_statement/get_balance_sheet/get_cash_flow pass the bare normalized symbol straight to the openbb-mcp tool call with no region qualifier); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P3_CHTR.json (income/balance/cashflow response bodies).
notes: Root cause: provider_registry.get_fundamentals() has a correctness gate (a Validator + an accept/fallback_ok pair) that prefers yfinance and rejects an incomplete/wrong openbb-mcp result — this is WHY the top-level /fundamentals/CHTR call correctly resolves to CHTR.BO (Chatterbox) via yfinance. get_income_statement/get_balance_sheet/get_cash_flow have no such gate (validate=None) and openbb-mcp is evidently the only/preferred provider for these three model-keys, so a bare 'CHTR' with no exchange-suffix resolution reaches the openbb-mcp tool and openbb resolves it to the globally best-known 'CHTR' — Charter Communications on NASDAQ — since the MCP surface likely has no coverage of BSE SME issuers at all. This is precisely the ticker-collision hostile trait this battery slot (P3) was designed to test (manifest.json:75-94: 'Ticker collides with Charter Communications'), materializing as a live, reproducible data-correctness bug rather than a mere documentation trap: any UI panel showing 'Financial Statements' / income-balance-cashflow for this Rs 54-crore Indian SME would silently render a $70B US cable company's numbers as fact, with the same nominal symbol and no error or divergence flag. Smallest fix shape: give get_income_statement/get_balance_sheet/get_cash_flow the same region-aware symbol resolution (or at minimum a correctness/region validator) that get_fundamentals already has, and/or have openbb_mcp_provider's normalize step append the resolved exchange suffix (as yfinance_provider._yahoo_symbol already does) before calling the MCP tool.

title: EPS and P/E for CHTR (Chatterbox Technologies) served ~14-19% off from three independent outside sources, with an internal inconsistency in the same response
repro: curl 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/CHTR' -> eps=7.41, pe_ratio=4.726046 (2026-09-19 snapshot). Outside truth: screener.in FY Mar2026 EPS=6.50 and BSE header EPS=6.51 (both close to each other); the battery manifest's own independently-curated reference (docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/manifest.json:82-89, as_of 2026-09-18) implies pe=5.38 at that day's price of 35.0, which only reconciles with an EPS near 6.50-6.51, not 7.41. Also: the SAME app response's own net_income_ttm/shares_outstanding = 90,980,000/14,143,800 = 6.43, close to the outside-sourced 6.50 and inconsistent with its own eps=7.41 field.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P3_CHTR.json (fundamentals call: eps=7.41, pe_ratio=4.726046, net_income_ttm=90980000.0, shares_outstanding=14143800.0); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P3_CHTR.json (eps_ttm=6.50, pe_ttm=5.84); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/manifest.json:82-89 (reference pe=5.38, price_inr=35.0); sidecar/services/yfinance_provider.py:297-395 (get_fundamentals takes info.get('trailingEps') at face value with no cross-check against info.get('netIncomeToCommon')/sharesOutstanding, unlike the debt_to_equity/dividend_yield fields immediately above/below it in the same function which DO get sanity-bounded or unit-normalised before being served).
notes: Principle: a served field should not contradict another field in the same payload. yfinance's trailingEps for this thinly-covered SME is stale or computed on a different share-count/period than netIncomeToCommon/sharesOutstanding in the identical response, and nothing in get_fundamentals cross-validates eps against net_income_ttm/shares_outstanding before serving it — the P/E ratio a user sees (4.73, 'this looks cheap') is materially lower than the true ~5.84-5.91, a wrong money-relevant number shown as fact with no flag. Smallest fix: in yfinance_provider.get_fundamentals, when both trailingEps and (netIncomeToCommon, sharesOutstanding) are present, sanity-check the ratio and prefer/flag a divergence beyond a small tolerance, or compute eps from net_income/shares as a fallback when yfinance's own trailingEps looks stale for a low-coverage small-cap.

title: Dividend fields (declared, trailing-12m paid, yield) served as blank/unavailable for CHTR even though the true value (zero, every year on record) is a knowable, sourced fact
repro: curl 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/CHTR' -> dividend_yield=null, dividend_per_share=null, dividend_per_share_ttm=null, each with field_meta.status='unavailable', field_meta.reason='provider did not publish this field'. Outside truth (screener.in Dividend Payout row) shows 0.00% every FY Mar2022 through Mar2026 -- the company has never declared a dividend since incorporation (2016); this is a determinable fact, not an unknown.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P3_CHTR.json (fundamentals.body.dividend_yield/dividend_per_share/dividend_per_share_ttm and their field_meta entries, all 'unavailable'); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P3_CHTR.json (dividend.last_declared_per_share=0, dividend.paid_trailing_12m_per_share=0, dividend.yield=0.00, all sourced to screener.in).
notes: A silent blank where the world has the value is exactly the mandatory subtle-tier check this pack was built for (declared vs paid dividends). A user researching this stock sees three blank dividend fields and cannot tell 'the company has never paid a dividend' apart from 'we don't have this data' -- both read the same in the UI, but only one is true and knowable. Smallest fix: when yfinance's info dict omits dividendRate/dividendYield entirely (as opposed to a legitimate null-because-zero shape yfinance sometimes uses), the app should distinguish 'provider silent' from a corroborated true-zero the way it already infers zero-dividend for issuers with a clean payout history in disclosures data, or at minimum flag the field as 'unconfirmed' rather than a bare unlabeled null in the UI.

title: debt_to_equity served as blank/unavailable for CHTR even though the company is genuinely debt-free (zero borrowings every FY on record)
repro: curl 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/CHTR' -> debt_to_equity=null, field_meta.status='unavailable', reason='provider did not publish this field'. Outside truth: screener.in standalone balance sheet 'Borrowings' = Rs 0.00 Cr at every FY-end shown (Mar2022 through Mar2026) -- the company is debt-free, D/E=0 is a determinable, sourced fact.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P3_CHTR.json (fundamentals.body.debt_to_equity=null and its field_meta); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P3_CHTR.json (debt_to_equity.value=0.00, sourced to screener.in balance sheet).
notes: Same class of defect as DAT-P3-3 (silent blank where the world has the value = medium per COMMON.md's severity scale), but note: because of DAT-P3-1, the app's OWN balance-sheet endpoint for this symbol is also unusable as a source of truth here (it returns Charter Communications' balance sheet, not Chatterbox's) — so today there is literally no in-app path to a correct CHTR debt figure at all. Fixing DAT-P3-1 (routing the balance-sheet call to the right company) would also give the app a real source for this field instead of the yfinance blank.

title: /disclosures/results is NSE-only by design and hard-502s for BSE-only/SME stocks, leaving zero results-calendar coverage for this battery slot's entire category
repro: curl 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/results?symbol=CHTR' -> HTTP 502, body {"detail": "nse_direct: 'CHTR' is not a known NSE instrument"}. CHTR is a real, actively-traded, correctly-resolved BSE SME stock (isin INE1B4801017, bse_code 544546) that simply has no NSE listing -- a legitimate, common case for the entire BSE-SME segment, not a bad symbol.
evidence: sidecar/routers/disclosures.py:73-89 (get_results: the symbol Query is documented and typed as 'NSE ticker, e.g. RELIANCE'; corporate_disclosures.get_results_calendar(normalized) raises ProviderError which is unconditionally turned into HTTPException(502, ...) with no BSE fallback or honest empty/'not applicable' path); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P3_CHTR.json (results_calendar call, status 502).
notes: Outside truth (the pack) DOES have a latest_results value for CHTR (H2 FY2025-26 half-year results, inferred filing_date 2026-08-25, sourced from BSE's announcement feed) -- the world has the data, the app's results-calendar endpoint just cannot reach it because it is hard-wired to NSE only. A 502 (server error) is also the wrong status for 'this exchange doesn't cover this instrument' -- it reads to a caller/UI as a backend fault rather than an honest 'no NSE results calendar for this BSE-only symbol.' Smallest fix: route BSE-SME/BSE-only symbols to a BSE-sourced results/board-meeting-outcome feed (the /disclosures/announcements endpoint already successfully surfaces board-meeting-outcome announcements for this exact symbol from BSE — see the announcements call in the same collected snapshot), or at minimum degrade to an empty 200 with a stated reason instead of a 502.
